message.content:
The drive from San Francisco to Los Angeles is roughly 380–400 miles (about 610–640 km) depending on the exact route you take. On a typical day, if you stay on the main interstate (I‑5 S) and drive at the posted speed limits, you can expect the trip to take around **6 to 7 hours**.

**Things that can affect the travel time:**

| Factor | Impact |
|--------|--------|
| **Traffic** | Heavy congestion in the Bay Area, especially during rush hours, can add 30 min–1 hour or more. |
| **Roadwork / Accidents** | Construction or incidents on I‑5 can cause delays. |
| **Speed Limits** | California’s speed limits vary (e.g., 55–65 mph on I‑5). |
| **Stops** | Refueling, food, or rest breaks add time. |
| **Weather** | Fog, rain, or storms can slow traffic. |

If you’re planning a trip, it’s a good idea to check a real‑time navigation app (Google Maps, Waze, Apple Maps) for current traffic conditions and estimated arrival times.
